 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 08:20:37 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 EPFO rule changes in 2026: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation has approved several changes to its withdrawal policies for EPF members. Members up to 55 years old can now withdraw up to 90% of their balance. The waiting period for EPF withdrawal after job loss has been significantly reduced from 12 months to 2 months. A Systematic Withdrawal Plan for EPF withdrawals has also been introduced to ensure regular income. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online EPF withdrawal rule changes In a decision that can benefit crores of subscribers, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ) has approved a proposal to reduce the minimum EPF balance requirement from 25% to 10% for members up to 55 years of age.
Following this change, these EPF members will be allowed to withdraw up to 90% of their corpus. The earlier withdrawal limit of the EPF corpus for the same age group was up to 75%. The eligibility to withdraw all 100% corpus at retirement, however, remains the same.
At its Central Board of Trustees (CBT) meeting today (Thursday, November 19, 2026), the EPFO has also cut the EPF withdrawal waiting period after job loss from 12 months to 2 months. 
Also Read: EPF SWP approved: Will it offer higher returns on monthly withdrawals than FDs, annuity? Know how your Rs 50 lakh corpus could grow 
Other than that, the EPFO has also approved the Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) withdrawal on retirement.
The CBT also gave in-principle approval to allow investment of up to 3% of fresh accretion in eligible Alternative Investment Funds. It has approved amendments to EDLI Scheme, 2026, to facilitate resolution of pending legacy exemption cases and provide a six-month window to eligible establishments for renewal of expired exemptions. Proposals concerning surrender of exemption by 27 establishments and cancellation of exemption in four establishments were reviewed.
However, the EPFO didn't announce any increase in the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS). It also didn't take any decision on whether it will approve higher EPS pension cases of all applicants.
 EPF members up to 55 years of age need to maintain 10% EPF balance now 
EPF subscribers now need to maintain a minimum of 10% of their EPF corpus till 55 years of age. Earlier, 25% of the EPF contribution needed to be retained.
Also Read: EPS-95 pension: Has government increased minimum EPS payout from Rs 1,000 per month? 
The full withdrawal of the entire PF balance (including the minimum balance) is allowed in case of retirement after attaining 55 years of age, permanent disability, inability to work, retrenchment, voluntary retirement or leaving India permanently, among others.
Sandeep Sehgal, partner-tax & valuations, AKM Global, said the EPFO board’s proposal to cut the minimum balance for partial withdrawals from 25% to 10% would give employees more flexibility to manage their finances, so that they can meet urgent expenses without resorting to high-cost borrowing.
"Once notified, the change would allow eligible members to withdraw up to 90% of their eligible PF balance, subject to the applicable conditions," says Sehgal.
 EPF withdrawal period after job loss cut 
The EPFO has also reversed its earlier decision of cutting the time from 12 months to 2 in case of job loss.
According to the earlier rule, in case of unemployment, 75% PF balance (that includes employer and employee contribution and interest earned) could be withdrawn immediately. The remaining 25% could also be withdrawn after one year.
Also Read: Higher EPS pension: Pensioners request Labour Ministry to withdraw EPFO circular rejecting exempted employees' higher pension claims 
A full withdrawal of the entire PF balance (including the minimum balance of 25%) was allowed for those retiring after attaining 55 years of age.
 SWP option for EPF withdrawals 
The CBT in its meeting today approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF withdrawals. The option will enable retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire amount in one go.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment said in a statement, "This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference. This facility would provide members with a structured source of periodic income while allowing the remaining corpus to continue generating returns."
The introduction of SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving the ownership of the underlying corpus.
The EPFO says that in case of the member's death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments.
Earlier, the SWP option was available to NPS subscribers. But now, EPF subscribers can also enjoy the facility.
 Relief in EDLI exemption cases 
The CBT has also approved amendments to EDLI Scheme, 2026, to facilitate resolution of pending legacy exemption cases. It has provided a six-month window to eligible establishments for renewal of expired exemptions, along with relief from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period.
"This will provide relief to eligible establishments by facilitating the settlement of pending and expired exemption cases, with a six-month window for renewal and relaxation from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period," the Labout Ministry says.
 Investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) 
The CBT in-principle approved to permit investment of up to 3% of fresh accretion in eligible Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), within the existing overall investment ceiling, initially through government-backed entities.
"The decision aims to diversify EPFO's investment portfolio while ensuring prescribed safeguards and investment oversight," the Ministry says.
 Surrender/cancellation of EPF exemptions 
The Ministry says that proposals concerning the surrender of exemption by 27 establishments and cancellation of exemption in four establishments were also reviewed in the meeting.
"These cases involve transfer of accumulated provident fund savings amounting to approximately Rs 5,996 crore to EPFO, covering 1,44,437 members, bringing their accounts under EPFO's direct administration," says the Ministry.
 Implementation of CITES 2.0 
The CBT was apprised of the progress of Centralised IT Enabled System (CITES) 2.0, a centralised, UAN-based digital platform developed by C-DAC to modernise EPFO services.
The Ministry says that post implementation of CITIES 2.0, auto-processing of claims increased from 39% to 71% of the total claim processed.
The introduction of pre-validation greater automation and simplified withdrawal limits reduced overall rejection ratio from 23% to 7.82%. The overall processing and the average claims settlement time has declined from 11.15 days to 2.57 days.
 Budget estimates 2026-27 and 2027-28 of EPFO 
The CBT also approved revised estimates for 2026-27 and budget estimates for 2027-28 of EPFO under EPF, EPS and EDLI Schemes, covering projected receipts, income and expenditure, to ensure effective financial planning and management of EPFO funds.
